There was natural vacuum of a good churrascaria place in Riyadh after the only one in the city has gone down the hill from quality standpoint. Set in upscale setting in modern crown Plaza hotel inside the Riyadh Digital City, Wildfire offered good cuts of meats and other salad and soup options. We were served by waiter John, who has been very helpful throughout the servings and was timely available for our needs at the table. As churrascarias are always heavy, we didn’t go to the desert round, however the salad and mains were great except for a few cults of meats that were a bit hard to chew, and the grilled pineapple was. It's been long overdue for me to visit Yautcha, and boy was i late to the party. The place is great with welcoming and attentive service, i tried the classic dim sum platter of 6 pieces, seabass one was nice, prawn was kind of dull, but the seafood black truffle was Wow. For the mains, i opted for Sanpei chicken, sweet and savoury with that lovely aroma of sweet basil, chicken was really tender. I also had the Singaporean vermicelli with prawns and squid, and i can't believe how soft that squid was, pure magic. I was disappointed that their mocktails were all unavailable because they looked great, and the drink I had was watered down and had no lemongrass flavour. I was too full for dessert but ordered it anyway, the pistachio cherry sesame, which unfortunately was a let down, the pistachio cremeaux was good, the cherry compote was too sour, the dates ice cream icy, but the biggest issue was the pasty which just didn't taste good, and the green stuff on the outside also, it was not an enjoyable dessert that i left half of it uneaten. Yautcha is a must visit with great ambience, food, and service. They just need better music lol

Located in the Mutal Complex, this Cafe Bateel location offers both indoor and outdoor seating. Once you enter, you are greeted immediately by friendly staff, who offer you direction to seating. The menu offers a great selection. This particular outing was for breakfast with a view. So we were seated on the terrace, with spectacular sea views. For drinks, we ordered freshly squeezed orange juice, Americano coffee and Saudi Latte. The Saudi Latte is a definite must try, made with the cafe's signature coffee (with cardamon), a shot of espresso, then topped with frothed with a hint of raw saffron. The aroma of this coffee is amazing, and is matched by its taste. For Breakfast, we ordered the Halloumi and Avocado toast and the Date French Toast. Before the drinks arrived, we were offered a basket of bread with sides of date butter and regular butter from France. The date butter is worth a try, it is subtle in favour and a perfect match with the fresh bread. The presentation of the breakfast was stellar. The plates were a perfect blend of colour and taste. I would highly recommend a visit, will definitely be back. Vegetarian options: Plenty of delicious options. Wheelchair accessibility: Elevator and ramp access to all the complex.

Bateel is a very high class restaurant. High profile people would usually dine into this place. The atmosphere is definitely worth something. Interior wise, very calm and luxurious. Especially where they have their chocolates and dates displayed. The food itself, the texture of the pasta is not the same as an ordinary pasta in a good way! Their pastas is very light yet it will make you full. Though the prices might be higher than usual restaurants, it’s definitely worth the try! Their desserts are top tier! The Cheesecake and as well as their tarts. I could say that everything was worth the price. What you pay for is what you get. Very welcoming staff too and the Head Chef is really nice and accommodating! Your Time won’t be wasted here! The food is very much Italian! Downside for some is that it is more on the high price line and it could seem intimidating, but still worth it!

Versatile Atmosphere: The restaurant caters to diverse preferences with both indoor and outdoor seating options, providing a great atmosphere suitable for various occasions. 7. Family-Friendly Atmosphere: The Cheesecake Factory further stands out as a great choice for families, offering a welcoming and accommodating atmosphere that enhances the overall dining experience.

Excellent experience. - Ambience: I enjoyed the vibes and the background music. The decor is on point and it’s got a very nice sea-view which I truly enjoyed with my family. - Food: excellent quality, unique presentation fits the concept, quality ingredients. The chocolate fondue dessert was nice as well. Very balanced, although I feel it needs more of salted caramel crumbs , the dessert felt it needs a bite kick of salt in it. - Prices: I found them fair for the experience this place has to offer. I’ve attached my bill. - Service: knowledgeable service team and very welcoming. What enjoyed the most: Passion mojito, Sweet corn and Kale Salad, Japanese Rice with wild mushrooms and truffle , the Grilled salmon. The Wagyu thing was nice but I wouldn’t comeback for it as well as the Shrimp tempura. The positive thing about the shrimp tempura is that it’s not greasy like most places. I will repeat the experience next time it will be dinner as I want to experience the night vibes. Thank you

Our reservation was made for brunch at 3pm on 26th of January, we came in to celebrate my husband’s birthday, but unfortunately it turned out to be a disaster. Service from reception was good upon arrival and our waiter was prompt in taking the order for us and explain which dishes we would be able to enjoy as we have some dietary requirements. Prawn crackers and water to start took already over 10 minutes to touch our table even though we were the only ones in the restaurant; from here, everything started to go downhill: Our appetisers (dim sum) took ages to arrive to then be left with an empty table for 50 minutes waiting for our mains, rice and noodles - upon checking we were served after 10 more minutes with our noodles and rice, waited an extra 15 minutes and then our first (out of 4!) main course finally came. At this stage our rice was already cold and we refused to get any more food since it already was 4:45pm and barely any food was served to us even though the whole place was empty until 4pm. My wife and I had a pleasant night out at Shang Plus. It was our first visit, and we ordered two appetizers and two main courses. The Wagyu pastry puff was delightful, but the Canadian lobster salad didn't quite meet our expectations. As for the main courses, the baked cod and Wagyu beef tenderloin were decent, although we found ourselves comparing them to other Asian restaurants in Jeddah. It felt like they could put in more effort to stand out. On a positive note, the mocktails, especially the blooming mojito, were amazing. The dessert, passion fruit creamperle, was also enjoyable. Additionally, we appreciated the friendly reception and attentive service from the waiter. The ambiance of the restaurant was pleasant, creating a nice dining atmosphere. However, it's worth noting that the prices were on the higher side.

Shang Palace is by far the best modern Chinese restaurant and only place in Jeddah that offers a glimpse into what real modern Chinese fine dining is all about. The ambiance is wow, beautiful carpets, wood panelled walls with traditional vases display and great lighting for the dining everywhere give it that intimate modern Chinese dining room feel. Kudos to the front of the house team and to the chef especially Chef Keith Yap he really passionate about making unforgettable food and great dining experience for each guest. The food is excellent, was there to try their new Shang Palace Dim Dum brunch series and were absolutely delighted with the food. It's unlimited course of dim sum, few mains in the menu to choose from and a dessert for closing of our meal. Loved all the dim sum and the Hong Kong style chicken. It's a must-try place, great for special occasions.

We love to provide you with the perfect evaluation for several places around specially breakfast restaurants because we have suffered alot when it comes to select a place for our Breakfast 🥞🍳, but most of the varieties around are not worthy of trying specially whatever the Social Media Parasitic Hoaxs advertise , only Pathetic Followers fall into such trap , that's why we want to provide an extremely honest experience for any place we attend to for the sake of awareness , so stay tuned... 1- Place and the design: They are trying their best to provide you with some European Vibes with the design and the colours but they failed dramatically which ended up with eye irritation, mood abuse and uncomfortable seats but still they have used such small space they have quite good 5/10. 2- The hospitality: The crew were good with their overwhelming welcome and care of all what we need following all the precautionary regulations for our safety and they were fast despite their confusion and unclear regulations towards Main Courses and Breakfast Menu 7/10. 3- Our order and the food quality: We have ordered Dolce De Lechi , Americano , Briggs , Berioche House Cured Salmon , the ingredients were 6/10 fresh, the look was nice with the Berioche delicious texture 7/10, the taste was delicious due to the Carbs effect 7/10, and the quality of the food for the Price 5/10 so far. 4- The experience conclusion: It was a fair experience, as we are talking here about simple ingredients with a specific bread 🍞 , also it's quite annoying to me that how come a place serve breads and don't have valid Coffee or Tea ☕ just sticking to the commercial types , which directly damage the quality of the experience , but despite all of that still a new experience that you can enjoy somehow , call it Carbs Dopamine Effect or the need for the Food industry to upgrade , which made it one of the good Breakfast Restaurants in Jeddah city in my opinion and if there is another, refer/share it so we can try it out 6/10. 5- The 𝕏-Score is: 42 / 70 1st- Ghanoj (closed) 2nd- Bay Rock 3rd- La Dolce Vita 4th- C.Taste 5th- Esquires 6th- I Hop (closed) 7th- American Corner 8th- Mazaq Zaman 9th- Beriosh     ✓ 10th- Shanashil 11th- Shobak 12th- Paul 13th- Fotur Faris We are trying our best to validate and evaluate all the restaurants from time to another with high end transparency and honesty so this result could be change from time to another and we will announce it... Vegetarian options: There is alot of great varieties for you there, so go and enjoy but be aware that Berioche have Dairies and Eggs 🥚 in order to be made. Dietary restrictions: This place is providing full Carbs products and ingredients that might cause you allergies so make sure to confirm on them any ingredients can cause you any allergies , and dont forget you hard workouts to burn all such high Calories 💪. Parking: Just come early in the morning and you will find quiet places to park.

This place was a unique experience despite some miscommunication with the staff. I had my order for take away, so I didn't have the in-restaurant eating experience. The menu has a variety and they are famous for thier pizza and pastas, I asked what's your best seller and he kept repeating these generas not specifying a dish name, I got thier best seller under the pasta category. The dish was ok as for taste, generous with amount, I couldn't finish it, expensive price, but due to the amount of food that is given I have to readjust the rating. Overall, this place is unique and as I said previously the amount of food they serve seems to be generous. My recommendation is to go there as a pair and share 2 dishes of your liking. Edit: recently I went to it and the quality of food has fallen down but the prices didn't my visit was to the pepsi street branch not the cornish branch. Served 4 pieces nicely sliced and is nice soft melt in your mouth. Definitely a winner if you crave slow roasted meat. Some good sides. Tried #onionrings thinly sliced and skin on fries were perfectly salted. They also serve asortment of #bakedbeans and #Mac and #cheese. If you're in Riyadh and craving the mouthwatering flavors of Texas-style BBQ, look no further! I recently had the pleasure of dining at this restaurant, and I must say, it exceeded all my expectations. As a BBQ aficionado with a deep appreciation for Texas BBQ, I was delighted to find beef ribs, briskets, and even a brisket burger on the menu. Each dish was a delightful explosion of flavors that took me straight back to the BBQ joints I love in Texas. The beef ribs were tender and perfectly seasoned, falling off the bone with every bite. The briskets were smoked to perfection, boasting that distinct smoky flavor I cherish. And the brisket burger, oh my! It was a brilliant fusion of BBQ goodness, and I couldn't get enough of it. The restaurant's ambiance was warm and welcoming, providing a comfortable setting to enjoy the fantastic meal. The staff was friendly, attentive, and knowledgeable about the dishes they served, which added to the overall dining experience. If you're a BBQ enthusiast like me or simply someone looking for an extraordinary culinary experience, this restaurant is a must-visit in Riyadh. I can't recommend it enough! Prepare your taste buds for a tantalizing journey through the flavors of Texas right here in Saudi Arabia.

The place was a delight in all aspects. The decor is lovely and comfortable. The music is chill and not too loud or overbearing, and the staff were great. We ordered the Shakshouka benedict, Briggs Sandwich, and the Salted Caramel French Toast. For the drinks we got the Homemade peach Ice tea and Rock Shaken. All the food was delicious. The shakshouka benedict’s garlic labneh sauce was a really nice touch. Especially with the toated bread with olives. It’s such an interesting and delicious take on a known dish. The briggs sandwich didn’t disappoint and is a nice order if you want something savory for breakfast. The salted caramel french toast was made even better with the addition of bananas suggestion courtesy of our great server Mr. Abdullah. I highly recommend this place and would definitely come again.

This was one of my best food experiences in Jeddah. We had no reservation, so we had to wait for a traditional setting to be available. We ordered the following: - Haemul Ramyeon (SR 55) - Noodle soup made with special seasoning in vegetable broth with seafood and vegetables - Haemul Dolsot Bibimbap (SR 85) - Hot stone pot bibimbap with stir-fried seafood and vegetables in rice mixed with savory soy sauce - Charcoal-Galbi Kimchi Fried Rice (SR 70) - Kimchi fried rice with charcoal grilled beef short-ribs marinated in BBQ sauce | Served with today's soup - Korean fried chicken boneless (SR 70) - Sweet and spicy (Yangnyeom) - Kimchi-Jeon (SR 70) - Spicy cabbage kimchi Korean pancake - Galbi-Gui (SR 95) - Grilled marinated short-ribs with soy sauce and ground vegetables, fruits Every order was a delight! The staff, with their warm and helpful nature, added to the charm of the place. Despite the slightly higher prices, the experience was definitely worth it.

The Cheesecake Factory is a very decent and good restaurant in Jeddah. The food is delicious, especially the cheesecakes, which are amazing. The pizza was good, though the size was rather small. Overall, the food quality is good, the taste is good but not outstanding as such, and the portion sizes are generous. My favorite item is the cheesecake, particularly the chocolate varieties. I've tried the Godiva Cheesecake, 30th Anniversary Cheesecake, and Hershey’s Cheesecake, all of which were excellent. Overall a good, a little pricey and very decent place to enjoy your dinner with your special ones.

Had a wonderful experience. We went for lunch. Took the lunch offer. We were 3 persons. Took one 89 riyal package and two 69 riyal package. In a package u can choose the main dish and each main dishe will come with a soup, salad,a loaf of bread and drinks. We had  delicious creamy broccoli soup( there was lentil and creamy broccoli soup, we choose brocolli soup), the salad options were green salad and Greek salad. Then there was one loaf of buttery delicous bushman bread which was tooo good. Soup and salad portion was enough. For drinks we can choose Pepsi 7 up etc or iced tea. Iced tea plain is included in the package, but if we need any flavors we need to pay 3 riyal etc. We took peach flavor which was really good. Drinks are refillable. For the main course we had brisket combo (89 riyal category) which included a moderate sized super delicious steak, grilled shrimps, and grilled chicken. It was tasting amazing. And a Tuscan smothered chicken and toowoomba chicken from 69 riyal category. All these main dishes u can choose whether it's to be served with grilled veg, french fries, rice or mashed potato as side.we choose 3 diff sides for our 3 main dishes so we could taste all. The prices are INCLUSIVE of tax. Food was amazing. I felt Toowoomba chicken a bit salty. That was the only flaw I could find. The ambience is nice, overlooking the fanateer beach.but surpsingly I found their tables a bit small , like if 4 adults sit on a table, it can a bit crampy. I don't know whether it's just my feeling 😜😜. They don't have separate cubicles for familes , if u want privacy u can ask and they will put that foldable partition panel near our table so we can enjoy our meals in privacy  . They have nice outdoor sitting area also. If the climate is good outdoor seating can be tried. The waiters were really good and helpful. They will even ask u the minutest details on how we would like our food to be served. Like whether we want the sauce to be served with the dish or separate. Over all a nice cozy experience. Check the QR code for menu. If you visit more than 4 times you can add it to your localty account and claim a free starter also.

This was an unexpected Chinese food trip and for years I have not revisited this place. I have forgotten why I didn't try it again but of course things change in time😆 and I'm happy one of my friends chose this.. For some comment that needs improvement, the place was too dark and the cutleries are not grip friendly.. it easily slips since the handle is like a chopstick and would have been better of it was flat. Overall this this restaurant deserves a try and   who knows could be your fave Chinese restaurant too.

My friends took me to Poke Bowl for a belated birthday dinner. When they said it was sushi in a bowl I wasn't too sure it would be good. But it was delicious! They have a bowl size for every appetite. I was really hungry so I got a large bowl. It was too much, but hey, I got leftovers🤤 the price was great for the quality and quantity of food you get. It is way cheaper than getting sushi at other places in Jeddah which, will ensure me coming back again. The environment was very clean and the decor was industrial meets beachside cafe. If you have been to Panda Express in the US it works in pretty much the same way. Very limited drink selection which could be much improved. They only had Sprite, Coke, Diet Coke, and 2 types of water.🙁 Make sure to finish dinner with a bowl of Matcha ice cream which was lovely.

This place is iconic, and for good reason. There is a serious level of dedication to the flavors produced here and every item on the menu was designed to make those flavors hit your taste buds. It’s technically a “Japanese” style of menu, but it’s fused with a pretty modern set of items that can suit anyone. They have sushi items, burgers, fish dishes, octopus, noddles etc. you won’t get bored. It is non alcoholic so keep this in mind - you’re there for the food and atmosphere anyway! A must try is the coal dish. The wait times can be problematic in the evenings, they do not accept reservations and so from 7pm onwards you’re basically on a wait list. The line seems to move pretty fast though. Ask the staff for recommendation, they are super helpful and kind. You’re going to have to go in with a specific budget in mind depending on the experience you’re looking for, so here is a bit of a guide: 1- two/three friends just hanging out over a few bites - AED150-200 2- four hungry people that want to feel satisfied but not overly full - AED550 - 600 3- five people or more that want to try at least 8 items (some special menu some regular menu) and feel satisfied - AED900 - 1,000 4- best culinary experience to try as many of the menu items as possible and feel satisfied - AED1,200+ Of course you can tailor your experience as you like, but it’s worth trying some of the staple basics as in the pictures I posted (all of that was approx AED 900, but we doubled up on some of those dishes and got drinks).

Who said healthy food can't be delicious?! As a self-proclaimed carnivore, I was initially sceptical about trying vegetarian Pan-Asian cuisine. But one visit to the beautiful Dip Dash in Barsha, and I was blown away! The food packs an authentic punch of flavour, despite being entirely vegetarian (not even egg!). I tried a variety of dishes, each with unique spices and textures. Here are some must-tries: 1.	Nigiri Mosaic: This visually stunning platter comes with nine pieces, each with unique ingredients and taste profiles. Can you imagine having jackfruit on a nigiri? Oh, it tastes so good! 2.	Pan-Fried Half Moon: These golden parcels are cooked to perfection and pair beautifully with Dip Dash's delicious homemade dips. The sauce I tried had a delightful kick, complementing the filling perfectly 3.	So Much Fudge: Chocolate lovers, rejoice! This dessert is pure indulgence without the guilt. The rich, creamy texture creates an unforgettable experience, you will want more for sure! 4.	Vanilla Panna Cotta: My personal favorite for its textural symphony. The smooth panna cotta melts in your mouth, while the nutty crumble adds a delightful contrast. I couldn't resist trying their Kimchi Rice and Multigrain Bao, and let me tell you, the photos I took don't do them justice! The jackfruit in the Bao had a delightful smokiness, and the rice was flavourful without being too spicy. Beyond the incredible food, the service at Dip Dash is exceptional. The staff is friendly and attentive, and the owner/manager is a lovely lady who passionately explains the restaurant's journey and helps you choose the perfect dishes from the menu. My conversation with her added a personal touch to the experience, making me feel truly welcome. If you're looking for an adventurous culinary journey with vibrant flavours, warm hospitality, and a commitment to delicious, plant-based cuisine, Dip Dash is a must-visit! Vegetarians and meat-lovers alike will be surprised and delighted. Trust me, you'll go back for more! PS: (This is not a paid review, I just really loved the food!! 😊)

What sets Saigon Vietnam Food apart is the attention to detail in each dish. The use of fresh ingredients and traditional cooking techniques truly pays homage to the authenticity of Vietnamese cuisine. It has outside seating with a lovely view of the water. Great setting for winter months. The pricing at Saigon Vietnam Food is reasonable, considering the quality and portion sizes. It's a great place to enjoy a flavorful meal without breaking the bank. We had the vegetarian mix platter, lemongrass chicken grill with vegan fried noodles. We had the house mocktail special which was really nice and a cold jasmine tea. The staff are really friendly and willing to take requests for allergy and taste preferences. Saigon Vietnam Food is a hidden gem in Dubai's culinary scene. If you're a fan of Vietnamese cuisine or simply looking to explore new flavors, this restaurant is a must-visit. With its welcoming ambiance, attentive service, and exquisite dishes, it offers an great dining experience that will leave you craving more. I recommend Saigon Vietnam Food for a taste of Vietnam in the heart of Dubai. Vegetarian options: Lots of options Parking: Depends on the rush...or else there are parking slots.

description: My friend and I decided to stop by this restaurant around 3pm after a tiring 3-hour walking tour, craving a hearty meal to rejuvenate us. We opted for their Jaforda salad and for entree chicken slices in creamy lemon sauce and stuffed chicken with rice, accompanied by two iced lattes to perk us up. The restaurant boasted a pleasant ambience with ample staff, all remarkably attentive. Our server seemed to be in training, but the manager's presence ensured smooth service throughout. The salad was delightful, although initially tangy, it complemented the chicken dishes impeccably. The chicken in creamy sauce was particularly savory, and the stuffed chicken, reminiscent of marinated rotisserie chicken, was bursting with flavor, accompanied by perfectly cooked rice. The portion sizes were generous, leaving us unable to finish everything. However, a few aspects dampened our experience. Firstly, the restaurant's policy of not serving tap water as an alternative to bottled water was disappointing. Despite my inquiry, the server insisted only bottled water was available, which felt unnecessary. Additionally, the automatic addition of a tip to the bill was unexpected, especially considering our recent dining experiences elsewhere. Lastly, while we opted to sit inside to avoid the heat and insects, the constant stream of flies due to the open door made for a rather bothersome dining atmosphere. Overall, while the food quality and service were commendable, the aforementioned issues detracted from an otherwise enjoyable meal experience.
restaurant_name: Askim Restaurant and Cafe (مطعم ومقهى أشكم)

description: My friend and I decided to stop by this restaurant around 3pm after a tiring 3-hour walking tour, craving a hearty meal to rejuvenate us. We opted for their Jaforda salad and for entree chicken slices in creamy lemon sauce and stuffed chicken with rice, accompanied by two iced lattes to perk us up. The restaurant boasted a pleasant ambience with ample staff, all remarkably attentive. Our server seemed to be in training, but the manager's presence ensured smooth service throughout. The salad was delightful, although initially tangy, it complemented the chicken dishes impeccably. The chicken in creamy sauce was particularly savory, and the stuffed chicken, reminiscent of marinated rotisserie chicken, was bursting with flavor, accompanied by perfectly cooked rice. The portion sizes were generous, leaving us unable to finish everything. However, a few aspects dampened our experience. Firstly, the restaurant's policy of not serving tap water as an alternative to bottled water was disappointing. Despite my inquiry, the server insisted only bottled water was available, which felt unnecessary. Additionally, the automatic addition of a tip to the bill was unexpected, especially considering our recent dining experiences elsewhere. Lastly, while we opted to sit inside to avoid the heat and insects, the constant stream of flies due to the open door made for a rather bothersome dining atmosphere. Overall, while the food quality and service were commendable, the aforementioned issues detracted from an otherwise enjoyable meal experience.
restaurant_name: Askim Restaurant and Cafe (مطعم ومقهى أشكم)

Very far from Japan (or even Asia, not even substandard ramen place in HK) level but some things are good. Tofu + eggplant starter 5/5: have seen one or the other in Japan, combining both very clever and super tasty. Best dish. Mocktails 5/5: very refreshing super tasty Octopus skewers 0/5: obviously burnt. Tastes burnt. Looks burnt. Weird a place would actually serve that. Chicken skewers 3/5: pretty good nothing special, too salty. Sushi fish rice 4/5: for Dubai really good, had some fatty tuna in there, yum yum. Ramen 3.8/5: nice to eat good ramen in Dubai, just nothing special again and also very salty. So, good for Dubai, but far from even a Shoryu in London. No point to even compare with Asia standard. Beef Tenderloin side 5/5: bravissimo 👌 Matcha parfait 2/5: served in an old wooden box. Ice cream on point. Matcha far too rich and not worth the calories. More like eating cake mix than a delicate dessert. Food overall too salty, and adds to the general experience of it not being clean. Cleanliness 0/5: it’s a Japanese place so again very weird. Take off shoes to then put my feet in an area which isn’t clean. Bathroom dust everywhere, probably used to be super nice but I just see dust on stuff that’s on the ground everywhere like toilet scrubber etc. again super weird, just clean the place guys come on. Japanese toilet very cool though. Price: would be more careful with ordering next time. Not really worth it in my opinion but that’s just me, people can like what they like it’s ok.

Great ambience and nice opportunity to get away from the hustle and bustle of the Atlantis hotel. Loved the aquarium view totally relaxing view of the marine. Food wise. Some controversial dishes I must say. I wasn’t a fan of the onion and mashmellow I just didn’t get it but my husband liked it! The “hot dog” tasted very average. My husband did not like the smoked salmon and caviar ball at all and found it sickening . The only dishes that stood out for both of us was the mushroom dish and the foie  which was cool. Mont  blanc desert, I did not like at all and gave it to my husband ( it tasted cheap and bland). The olive desert was interesting and a nice experience. We also liked the red mullet dish but again not mind blowing. I like the urchin dish and the oyster (husband didn’t). They did bring out cake with candle for my birthday which was nice and a gift to take home which I loved. Highlight of it was the chef coming to greet us which was lovely. Finally the non alcoholic drinks were not good at all sorrrry. So overall some interesting dishes ( mushroom, foie, urchin and olive) some medium like the red mullet and some poor tasting ( onion, mont blanc, smoked salmon) . Nevertheless we enjoyed our night and had a great experience.

A top choice for an authentic Vietnamese restaurant in Dubai. The menu covers some very iconic Vietnamese dishes then adds some of their own creations that are somewhat fusion or modified for the local market but grounded in Vietnamese cuisine and flavours.  On the drinks side you should look out for Vietnamese coffee if you like a strong and sweet robusta coffee, and bubble tea which for a non-specialist with very limited variety is OK. The food is overall excellent with fresh ingredients, balanced flavours and textures, and many of the dishes are quite healthy.  This restaurant definitely rates highly for delicious Vietnamese food in Dubai. Service (from the entirely Vietnamese staff when I was there) is friendly and very pleasant to deal with.  There's some tables indoors but even more outside that, given it's upstairs on the balcony, has good views over the lake.

description: What we ordered: Bosporus Mixed Grill + Plain White Rice. Our experience: As a starter for our lunch, we were served a giant airated flat bread topped with sesame seeds. It also came with a small serving of well-prepared hummus as a dipping sauce. This was a simple dish and the combination worked well as an appetizer. A while later we were served the mixed grill dish that was richly spiced and mouth - wateringly aromatic (I believe it was the parsley). The meat we were served was fresh, tender, and juicy, and the leftover hummus from earlier added to the already spectacular taste palette of the whole dish. I'm not sure what else went into preparation of the hummus other than chickpeas, but I'm certain it can take your plain white rice to another level (bc that's what it did for us!). When we were done with our main course, we were served complimentary black teas (I don't know if it was Turkish tea or just regular tea), and oh what a delight they were! It is served without any sugar so you can enjoy it as you please. It made dining here feel like such a treat and what better way to wrap up a lunch from here? It was our first time trying Turkish cuisine and all in all, we had a positive experience. Highlights: (1) Our waiter, who was educated and aware enough to adjust our service and orders to accommodate my gluten intolerance. She did her best to keep me safe from allergens and to keep cross contamination to a minimum (2) The complimentary bread+hummus and tea. Suggestion: Generally speaking, all of our stomachs would be happier if the serving sizes were upgraded to include some more in quantity, especially with the grills.
restaurant_name: Bosporus Turkish Cuisine - The Dubai Mall - مطعم بوسبورس دبي مول

description: Nestled in the heart of Difc, Mamaesh Restaurant offers a delightful culinary journey into Palestinian cuisine. Known for its warm hospitality and authentic flavors, Mamaesh captures the essence of traditional Palestinian dishes with a modern twist. The highlight of our dining experience was undoubtedly the fatayer, savory pastries filled with a variety of ingredients like spinach, cheese, or minced meat. Each bite was a perfect blend of crispiness and flavorful fillings, showcasing the chef's expertise in pastry making. Accompanying our meal was a refreshing salad, bursting with freshness and vibrant colors. The ingredients were evidently sourced with care, enhancing the overall dining experience. For the main course, we indulged in the chicken zatar wings, a tantalizing dish marinated in a blend of aromatic spices and herbs. The chicken was tender and infused with the distinctive flavors of zatar, leaving a memorable taste on the palate. No Palestinian meal is complete without freshly baked bread, and Mamaesh excels in this department. The bread served was warm, soft yet perfectly textured, complementing every dish it accompanied. The ambiance at Mamaesh is cozy and inviting, ideal for both intimate dinners and gatherings with friends or family. The staff was attentive and knowledgeable, offering recommendations that added to our enjoyment. In conclusion, Mamaesh Restaurant stands out for its commitment to authenticity and quality. Whether you're a connoisseur of Palestinian cuisine or a newcomer eager to explore new flavors, Mamaesh promises a culinary adventure that won't disappoint. I look forward to returning soon to savor more of their delightful offerings.
restaurant_name: Mama'esh DIFC Central Park Towers ممائيش أبراج سنترال بارك

We had a phenomenal experience at Hakkasan, thanks to our amazing server, Soe. We started with the boneless Peking duck, which was perfectly crispy on the outside and tender inside, bursting with rich flavors that set the tone for the meal. For the main course, we had the Peking duck with bone, which was equally delicious and expertly prepared, offering a deeper, more robust flavor. The stir-fry veggies were fresh and crisp, perfectly seasoned, complementing the richness of the duck. The hand-pulled noodles were a highlight, with a perfect texture and delightful taste that paired wonderfully with the other dishes. We finished the meal with their famous spiked lemon, a refreshing and tangy dessert that was the perfect end to our meal, and Chinese tea, which was aromatic and soothing, recommended by Soe. The experience truly felt like a Michelin-star experience because of Soe's exceptional service and attention to detail. We left feeling valued and well taken care of. Highly recommend giving Hakkasan a try for an unforgettable dining experience!

I was totally excited to finally have the opportunity to try out this well-known franchise during my trip to Abu Dhabi. Making my reservation was easy - I made mine via google map and got it confirmed immediately. The location of the restaurant was pretty odd - it’s located down a long corridor after a bank branch, and three souvenir shops within the large Emirates Mall; one wouldn’t expect a high end restaurant to be located near these. Service was within my expectations. However I rated this a 3-star as all my dim-sum was brought out immediately before I could even start to finish a bite. This meant that (1) my table was filled to the max (2) my food got cold before I could even try it (3) visually, it made me so full Food was also within my expectations but nothing spectacular. Nothing out of the ordinary that a dim sum restaurant in Singapore could not make. Would I return? Yeah maybe..  but I would not give it a Michelin star.

description: My visit to Bosporus in Abu Dhabi Mall for breakfast was an experience I'll cherish for a long time. This restaurant is a slice of culinary heaven, offering a taste of Ottoman cuisine that is both authentic and exceptionally delicious. The Ottoman breakfast was a standout. Each dish was a revelation of flavors and textures, perfectly capturing the essence of traditional Turkish cuisine. The ingredients were fresh, the presentation was impeccable, and every bite was a delightful journey through rich and aromatic flavors. It was evident that the chefs at Bosporus are masters of their craft, dedicated to delivering an authentic and memorable dining experience. The ambiance of the restaurant added to the overall enjoyment of our meal. The decor at Bosporus is a beautiful blend of modern and traditional Turkish elements, creating an atmosphere that is both elegant and inviting. It's a setting that transports you, making you feel as if you've stepped into a charming eatery in the heart of Istanbul. The staff at Bosporus deserve special mention for their exceptional service. They were attentive, friendly, and went above and beyond to ensure our dining experience was perfect. Their knowledge of the menu and recommendations were spot on, adding a personalized touch to our meal. In conclusion, Bosporus in Abu Dhabi Mall is a must-visit for anyone looking for an exquisite breakfast experience. The combination of delectable food, a wonderful atmosphere, and outstanding service makes this restaurant a standout. It's a place where the flavors of Turkey are brought to life, leaving you with a desire to come back for more.

We had a great time, paid our bill, and left. However, in the next store, I saw that my shirt was covered in pulls and completely ruined. I returned to the restaurant and showed it to the manager, Ahmed. His initial reaction was to say that all their chairs are smooth and he couldn't believe this happened. Eventually, he offered me a piece of cake, probably for free, but we were too full to eat anything else. He didn't offer any other solution, though I would have accepted a voucher for a future visit. Unfortunately, such an offer was not made, and the evening was ruined. I was disappointed with the way this situation was handled. I hope the restaurant improves its customer service and attention in the future.

Turkish cuisine, famously known for its kebabs and köfte, it is actually so much, much more! Bosporus is a great spot for Turkish food! Well worth a visit if you are looking for authentic Turkish and Mediterranean food. We had a lovely lunch and everything was spot on. From the moment we walked in we felt very welcomed. Great hospitality and service! Our food, especially my lahana sarma, mix dolma and salad all served together with Turkish bread-Simit (a circular bread, typically encrusted with sesame seeds or curekot / nigella sativa ) and no-knead bread (flat, fluffy traditional bread usually topped with sesame seeds, sometimes with pul biber, either way it’s just delicious!) The attentive and friendly service by Murat and Noor was top notch! Unfortunately they didn’t have my favourite sahlep but instead I’ve had creamy delicious sutli with pistachios along with the famous Turkish çay served in a tulip-shaped glass called ince belli! Very nice authentic experience!
restaurant_name: Bosporus Turkish Cuisine - Abu Dhabi Mall - مطعم بوسبورس أبوظبي مول

We chose this eatery as we were passing by. My family was seated in the curtained booths and the restaurant was oozing a great Indian atmosphere. We ordered two whole tandoori chickens, a gosht biriyani, a butter chicken biriyani and a plethora of little nibbles. To break our fast, they provided Laban and a small fruit selection containing grapes, melons, dates and nuts. Beginning with the tandoori chickens, they came on a naan bread bed. The chicken had a slight spicy kick to it that elevated it from boring to elite level. Most importantly, my kids rated it 10/10. The butter chicken biryani was delicious. It arrived on a large plate served with a pot of butter chicken sauce on the side. There were plenty of chicken tikka pieces and the whole combination was top notch. My wife had the gosht biryani, which was served in a sealed pot. The mutton was cooked to perfection and the flavour was outstanding. My son said the naan bread were some of the best he’s had and took some extra ones with him. The staff were absolutely fantastic, they delivered a perfect service that we felt obliged to mention our satisfaction to the Manager. I would highly recommend this restaurant highly to anyone looking for delicious Indian food. Kid-friendliness: The staff were very friendly to our children and seated us away from the busy parts

Disappointing food at a very high price point. I was really excited to try the spot because of the great reviews. But both my friend and I felt the food was a huge miss. We ordered dahi puri, butter chicken, paneer tikka masala, chili cheese naans, and a mango lassi. Very standard and typical menu items to judge an Indian restaurant by. And we’re both not picky eaters. The mango lassi simply wasn’t good - my friend couldn’t drink it past two sips. It had a strange flavor which was neither sweet nor tangy. The dahi puri and complimentary papads were probably the best thing we had all night. Savory and well seasoned. The butter chicken had 3-4 pieces of chicken, and just didn’t taste like much. Same with the paneer tikka masala. They’re typically such flavorful dishes but the combination of seasoning and the preparation at India Palace just fell flat for us. They just did not taste great. The chili cheese naan was quite appetizing though - it was one of the only saving graces of the curry dishes. In the end, we paid almost 200 AED for food that missed the mark. There’s way better Indian food throughout the Dubai and Sharjah areas that you should opt for over this spot.

description: Sometimes you eat out; sometimes you have a dining experience! This is the latter. Although it is Indian food, the cuisine is different than what you might think. Even dishes with the same name (e.g. palek paneer) are flavored uniquely. And by unique, I also mean tasty!! Sweet. Savory, spicey. Mild. Everything. And at 40 AED a person for everything, it's a noteworthy deal! The service was incredible too, including detailed stories about the food and its uses in Rajastanian culture (see video I posted). Plus, it's an all you can eat scenario! They insist on keeping your little bowls of food filled. I almost couldn't walk out. Too full. The location is in classic dusty, wild, non-fancy Sharjah. In my opinion, this only adds to the global feel of the experience. This place earns Dr. Matt's stamp of approval! Vegetarian options: It's all vegetarian Kid-friendliness: They are welcoming of kids! Big time
restaurant_name: Rajasthan Al Malaki - Restaurant مطعم راجستان الملكي

Having never been to a Raclette Night till date, this was a new experience for me. With 3 glasses of wine and a raclette platter per person at AED. 189, I found that quite reasonable considering that most of the time, a glass of wine costs anything between AED. 40-60! We choose to sit outdoors - to enjoy the lovely music as well as the weather. We started off with a glass of red wine from Chile. It wasn't a sweet wine, and that was a great choice as I had the server choose it for me. Next, we were served with a molten raclette on sauteed ratte potatoes with beef chorizo on the side. While the beef chorizo was super juicy and delicious, what made me love this dish was the perfectly cooked potatoes topped with cheese. The cheese literally melted into the potatoes cracks and it was the best basic potatoes I have ever eaten. I could not wait longer for the platter of cold cuts and cheeses, so we requested for the same along with our second glass of wine, white wine this time. The platter consisted of walnuts, prunes, figs, cold cuts of beef and chicken, along with a variety of cheese and crackers. A fresh plate of bread was provided on the side. If you're a vegetarian like my friend who joined me, you can still enjoy this platter as long as you have a companion who loves meat along with you! The crackers with cheese and the beef cold cuts made for a delicious cracker! Everything was great, and worth every dirham, for real! As this offer does not provide any desserts, we went ahead with Valrhona Chocolate Pecan and Caramel Bar. Filled with milk chocolate mouse, this dessert was a wonderful ending to the night.

When it comes to traditional fish cuisine, Babel Bahr stands out as a true gem in Lebanon. The restaurant excels in every aspect, offering a unique dining experience that sets it apart from typical seafood establishments. One of the standout features of Babel Bahr is their authentic charcoal-grilled fish, a method that truly caters to the discerning palate of gourmet enthusiasts. Unlike the common gas or electric grilling methods, the use of real charcoal imparts a distinctive flavor and aroma to the fish that elevates the dining experience. For an authentic taste of the region, I highly recommend trying the local fish varieties such as Ajaj, Braq, or Gazaleh, which are seasonal delights typically available until late summer. These fresh catches truly showcase the rich flavors of Lebanese seafood. To complement your grilled fish, be sure to pair it with a glass of their excellent local Arak. The combination of grilled fish and Arak creates a harmonious blend of flavors that is sure to delight your taste buds. Overall, Babel Bahr offers a culinary experience that is not to be missed for seafood aficionados looking to savor the best of Lebanese fish cuisine. From the charcoal-grilled delicacies to the superb local drinks, a visit to Babel Bahr promises a memorable dining experience. Cheers

First time here - my husband has been going on about this place for months, but it isn't very cost effective. So I thought he would be thrilled to go here for his birthday. Made reservations via WhatsApp - for the Medieval dinner for Two + drinks - 699AED. Gave our order atleast an hour in advance and accepting to push our reservations as we were running a bit late after work. Now... First impressions, the location itself was a bit tricky to find, it was remote and dark. Once we found it we parked at the free parking space and went in. It definitely embraces the Viking theme, the entrance has a small area adorned with intricately carved viking motifs. Our host was Sergey, quirky/energetic. We were led to the main dining area, which was lit with a few dimmed chandeliers, wooden tables and benches, with faux stoles. Offcourse, the table itself was matching to the theme with dimly lit candles and a somewhat disproportionate dinner plate and utensils. The ambiance was quite nice but I'm a little aversed to eating at a place where I can't really see my food, sensory stimulus aids to the experience after all. Now the 5 course meal, enjoyable but lacked in certain consistencies. The amuse-bouche was crunchy but a little bland. The meat salad was delish but the triquetra was a disappointment. French onion soup was lush. Now our main course, was a mix of all 5 dishes, One piece of the chicken was dry and bland while the other was succulent. My husband enjoyed the meats(ribeye/lamb). The salmon was dry/lacked flavor, but the oven-grilled eggplant was surprisingly delectable. Finally the dessert, the apple pie knockoff dish, which was plated out to wish my husband (which I'm grateful for), the pastry was burned, but it was definitely more palatable then the cheesecake like, somewhat questionable option. I won't question the quality of the produce itself, which I do believe meets standards, but the flavor profile was off putting. Additionally, we had ordered the lava cheese bread (good cheese pull) and the moon pie(basically over fried potato wedges without any flavoring). The drinks, they didn't have diet options for soft drinks so we chose the fruit drinks believing it to be freshly made - but no. The pineapple was alright but I do believe the orange juice was spoilt(had a strange metallic taste) - we asked for it to be changed immediately. Our servers were pleasant, but seemed a little distracted. My husband and I thoroughly enjoyed the performances. The final bill with the service fee and tax , the Fazaa discount came to about 728 AED. I must admit that I found the final bill to be a bit higher than expected for the Average joe ,but I wanted to treat my husband to an experience. However, I believe that ensuring a balance between cost, customer service and value would enhance the overall appeal of this place. Conclusively, a One - time must visit.

We loved this steak house, and this was the first we liked in Lebanon. Casual and trendy.  Great idea for a specialty grill with four main dish items on the menu. With fries or baked potato, Lulu lettuce salad, butter/herb sauce for steak, which service advised was good also for baked potato.  It wasn't. We ordered daily special rib eye for 2 for more than twice the cost of a single dish  but wasn't enough for two. But very tasty Columbian beef rather than Brazil beef. Looked more like an awesome prime rib steak, which Londoners serve with Yorkshire Pudding. Here's an idea for this restaurant. Want free recipe? French fries with steak? Come on! And fries were less than ordinary. The baked potato was also mediocre - more boiled than baked. Butter with herbs was a fail for us. Try butter alone, or with little garlic. Or just get some sour cream and toast the potatoes well for five stars. Our steak had a rib bone with stringy meat near the bone that was raw since near the bone, but that was the nature of this steak, except the second person had a smaller share. Nevertheless, we loved the place and the food. Our critique points are hopeful suggestions so we can make this place a regular. Also, should have mustard options - English hot mustard from powder, Dijon variety, BBQ or other easy off the shelf condiments or sauces. Loved the experience enough to comment.

Uptown Beirut, located in Dbayeh, Lebanon, is a vibrant and bustling restaurant that offers a diverse menu featuring a wide range of dishes from various cuisines. As you enter the restaurant, you are greeted with a warm and welcoming ambiance, coupled with friendly staff ready to assist you throughout your dining experience. The menu at Uptown Beirut is extensive, catering to different tastes and preferences. Starting with the salad section, the Grilled Halloumi Salad stands out as a delightful combination of fresh iceberg lettuce, rocca, cherry tomatoes, black olives, and balsamic dressing, topped with perfectly grilled halloumi cheese and pesto sauce. The flavors and textures blend harmoniously, creating a refreshing and satisfying salad. For those seeking a unique flavor experience, the Chicken Avocado Sandwich is a must-try. The tender chicken breast marinated in flavorful spices is perfectly complemented by the richness of avocado. Served on a sandwich white bread with garlic mayo sauce, fresh iceberg lettuce, and a side of crispy French fries, this sandwich is a delightful combination of flavors and textures. If you're in the mood for pasta, Uptown Beirut offers a range of options. The Pasta Al Pesto is a classic choice, featuring al dente pasta tossed in a fragrant pesto sauce, enhanced with fresh cream and grated Parmesan cheese. The dish is beautifully balanced, allowing the vibrant flavors of the basil and garlic to shine through. Uptown Beirut also excels in its grills section. The Chich Tawouk, marinated chicken skewers, is a popular choice among diners. The juicy and tender chicken is grilled to perfection, accompanied by fresh tomatoes, onions, and Arabic bread. The dish is elevated by the aromatic garlic paste and chili bread, adding a delightful kick to each bite. The dessert selection at Uptown Beirut is equally impressive. The Molten Cake is a chocolate lover's dream. The warm, gooey chocolate center is encased in a moist and decadent cake, creating a delightful contrast of textures. Each bite is a heavenly experience that leaves you craving for more. To complement the dining experience, Uptown Beirut offers a wide range of beverages, including refreshing fresh juices, soft drinks, and a selection of hot beverages like Lebanese coffee and cappuccino. The service at Uptown Beirut is attentive and efficient, ensuring that your needs are met promptly and with a smile. In summary, Uptown Beirut in Dbayeh is a fantastic dining destination that offers a diverse menu, delicious flavors, and a welcoming ambiance. Whether you're in the mood for a refreshing salad, a satisfying sandwich, a comforting pasta dish, or a mouthwatering grilled meal, Uptown Beirut has something to satisfy every craving. With its attentive service and a wide range of beverage options, Uptown Beirut provides a memorable dining experience that will leave you wanting to come back for more.

We were promptly guided to an available table. Our order comprised various appetizers. The crispy salmon salad, while featuring fresh salmon, could benefit from an added crunch and a more pronounced flavor profile. As a sweet conclusion, we indulged in the oreo tempura, which proved to be a dazzling delight. On the whole, our experience at Ginger & Co was highly enjoyable. I wholeheartedly recommend giving it a try, especially if you're looking for a lively dining establishment in the Hazmieh vicinity.

We also tried their Chicken Tandoori (Bhatti Ka Murgh) and that too was delicious. I was very happy that the chicken was cooked right to the bone and wasn't chewy or tough. Kudos to them for the preparation style. It would be great if they could do away with red food colouring on the Tandoori. The Tandoori roti too was very soft. If you aren't a fan of spicy preparation, please inform them while ordering as Deccan dishes can be heavy on the chillies. We enjoyed the spices though. We will definitely return to try more of their preparations.

Society Bistro stands out as a delightful dining spot known for its appealing ambiance and delicious meals, all at remarkably low prices. The restaurant is typically full, making it essential to book in advance or be prepared to wait for a table. Although the service can sometimes seem distracted due to the crowd, the overall atmosphere remains charming, romantic, and somewhat elegant. It's notably impressive how the bistro manages to offer food of such quality at a fraction of the cost compared to similar bistros. Recently, there's been a slight dip in quality, yet the offerings remain good. Our meal included a quinoa Scamorza salad, which was generous though lacking in originality. The poulet au citron was excellent, but you can barely taste the lemon. The truffle burger and fondant au chocolat were enjoyable, yet neither dish stood out as exceptional. I endorse this restaurant for its excellent cuisine, charming French atmosphere, and unbeatable prices.

Dar al Amar is in the heart of Tripoli at Dam w Farez street. The menu at Dar al Amar offers a wide variety of Lebanese dishes, from mouthwatering mezzes to hearty mains and delectable desserts. Each dish is prepared with care and attention to detail, showcasing the rich culinary heritage of Lebanon. In addition to the delicious food, the service at Dar al Amar is top-notch. The staff is friendly, attentive, and knowledgeable about the menu, making recommendations based on your preferences. The overall dining experience is enhanced by the welcoming atmosphere and the genuine care shown by the team. Overall, Dar al Amar is a must-visit Lebanese restaurant in Tripoli, North Lebanon. Whether you are a local resident or a visitor to the area, this restaurant offers a culinary journey that celebrates the essence of Lebanese cuisine. I highly recommend Dar al Amar for a memorable dining experience that will leave you

restaurant_name: Rajasthan Al Malaki - Restaurant مطعم راجستان الملكي

description: The restaurant is mid-sized, we felt it was a bit cramped. The tables were adorned with Rajasthani art work and the walls were filled with Rajasthani paintings. Rajasthan Al Malaki offers vegetarian food, special shout-out to their Thali. On weekends they have special thali- Royal Thali.  Thalis are served with Chaas or Flavored Indian buttermilk. We also had their special Lassi. It was delicious, thick, sweet and creamy, which was not part of the thali though… We were served 2 types of starters, Kaddi and Rice, 4 types of vegetables, 3 types of Roti, 2 types of sweets and popular Rajasthani dishes like Dal Baati Churma, Gatte Ki Sabji, Pachkuute Ka Saag  and Dahi Vada and everything was lip smacking. Only kacha parking spots available, since it was our first visit to this restaurant we found it quite challenging to arrive here even after pinning the location on Google map, as on all sides the road construction was in progress. Regular Rajasthani Thali- Sunday to Thursday : 25 Dhs per person Weekend(Royal) Rajasthani Thali- Friday & Saturday: 30 Dhs per person Kids under 8- Half Price Location- Behind DPS Sharjah Primary School, Muwailih Commercial, Sharjah

It was delicious, thick, sweet and creamy, which was not part of the thali though… We were served 2 types of starters, Kaddi and Rice, 4 types of vegetables, 3 types of Roti, 2 types of sweets and popular Rajasthani dishes like Dal Baati Churma, Gatte Ki Sabji, Pachkuute Ka Saag  and Dahi Vada and everything was lip smacking. Only kacha parking spots available, since it was our first visit to this restaurant we found it quite challenging to arrive here even after pinning the location on Google map, as on all sides the road construction was in progress. Regular Rajasthani Thali- Sunday to Thursday : 25 Dhs per person Weekend(Royal) Rajasthani Thali- Friday & Saturday: 30 Dhs per person Kids under 8- Half Price Location- Behind DPS Sharjah Primary School, Muwailih Commercial, Sharjah

I visited this place after 22 years from initially going there. Little has changed in terms of the setup. One major plus is being smoke-free. Even vapes are frowned upon. I tried two dishes, chicken with cheese and chicken with lemon. They both come with oven roast potatoes and a side of salad. Portion size is very generous. They could easily trim the portions by a third and reduce the prices accordingly which are on the high side for Tripoli. The food presentation is nothing to write home about. In terms of flavour, it was a let down. The chicken with cheese was salty, creamy, lacking any chicken taste. The chicken with lemon needs to have less/no artificial lemon flavouring. Maybe they are using concentrated lemon juice. The oven potatoes tasted and looked great but they were way hotter than the chicken in terms of temperature. And because of their proximity to the side salad, the salad became lukewarm. I should point out that they serve a freshly backed loaf of bread with black olives. The olives come with vegetable oil or so it seems, ruining this experience from the get go. The bread is way too salty. The staff were prompt and courteous. The smoke-free environment. These two saved the day. The bathrooms are well kept. Expect to pay for valet parking even if you park yourself. Parking: You could park up the hill away from the restaurant and take a short stroll if weather permits.

description: Place is a small restorant located near the main roads of jal el dib. With few locations to park and a valet service. You are welcomed with friendly staff. Locations require reservation since they are always crowded. At the time of the visit, the place was crowded. Food took a while to be served. Hummus: was good freshly made Fattouch: lacks cucumbers and tomato came with big uncut green vegetables ( not fresh) Sanbusik: came fried and well drained from oil, thin and crusty, but meat insert lacks flavour. Spicy fries: well fried and came dried from oil crusty and good spicy combination. Tawook platter: was about 2 shish of tawook with nothing else. Was well cooked jucy and well done. Meat wrap: meat was well done and cooked, wrap came with meat hummus and few green vegetables, with lot of bread. Despite the excess, it was tasty. Plase is known for his grill. They are always on point, but latley can be considered as pricy since portions are getting smaller. Place is recommended for a takeout since atmospheres in restaurants are not the best too noisy and crowded. Vegetarian options: There are some vegetarian options Dietary restrictions: They have option for dietary persons with grilled options are the best. Parking: Parking is hard to find, can park around 8 cars in front of restaurant which are almost always occupied Kid-friendliness: No kids menue Wheelchair accessibility: It is easily accessible since the restaurant is located at street level
restaurant_name: Abou Jihad Restaurant Jal el Dib

description: One of the best lebanese-cuisine restaurants in price/quality ratio to date. It’s true that the atmosphere is nothing fancy, but the good-quality and fairly-priced food is definitely worth it. It is also one of the most consistent places in quality and taste over the years. I have been going there close to 10 years and it managed to maintain high level of consistency. Recommended dishes: generally all Lebanese mezzeh items (tapas) but also grilled meat, kabak and chicken taouk. The tablouleh, fattoush and rocca zaatar salads are always fresh and tasty. I also like in particular how they make the traditional lebanese dish of fouwerigh (the only place I have it outside my mom’s kitchen!). Vegetarian options: Plenty of vegetarian options

I recently had the pleasure of dining at O&C, and I must say it was an exceptional experience. Without a doubt, O&C is the best sushi place in Lebanon, offering the most trusted and amazing fish quality you can find. One of the standout features of O&C is their generous sushi portions. Unlike many other sushi places, O&C doesn't skimp on the fish. It's not all rice; you can expect a generous amount of fish in each sushi roll, making every bite a delight. The value for money at O&C is truly remarkable. For around $35, you can enjoy their open sushi option, where you can indulge in a wide variety of sushi rolls. If you prefer a la carte, you can enjoy a whopping 35 pieces of sushi for just $50. This is an amazing deal considering the high quality and freshness of the fish. While the food at O&C is exceptional, I must mention that the service can be a bit slow. It took quite a bit of time for our sushi to arrive, which was a slight inconvenience. However, once the sushi arrived, it was definitely worth the wait. I hope that O&C can improve on this aspect and provide a more efficient service in the future. Additionally, I noticed that the customer service at O&C could be better. The waiters seemed somewhat distant and lacked enthusiasm. They appeared to be a bit sad, low on energy, and sometimes even lazy. Improving the friendliness and attentiveness of the waitstaff would greatly enhance the overall dining experience at O&C. Overall, I highly recommend O&C for their exceptional sushi offerings and the incredible value for money. Despite the minor drawbacks in service, the delicious and high-quality sushi more than makes up for it. Visit O&C for an unforgettable sushi experience in Lebanon.

If you prefer a la carte, you can enjoy a whopping 35 pieces of sushi for just $50. This is an amazing deal considering the high quality and freshness of the fish. While the food at O&C is exceptional, I must mention that the service can be a bit slow. It took quite a bit of time for our sushi to arrive, which was a slight inconvenience. However, once the sushi arrived, it was definitely worth the wait. I hope that O&C can improve on this aspect and provide a more efficient service in the future. Additionally, I noticed that the customer service at O&C could be better. The waiters seemed somewhat distant and lacked enthusiasm. They appeared to be a bit sad, low on energy, and sometimes even lazy. Improving the friendliness and attentiveness of the waitstaff would greatly enhance the overall dining experience at O&C. Overall, I highly recommend O&C for their exceptional sushi offerings and the incredible value for money. Despite the minor drawbacks in service, the delicious and high-quality sushi more than makes up for it. Visit O&C for an unforgettable sushi experience in Lebanon.

I had to write a review about Provincial in Antelias because it was just fantastic! We ordered a whole bunch of stuff to share, and everything was so fresh, it felt like they picked it straight from the garden. The salads were incredible. We got a quinoa salad and a kale salad, and the dressings were delicious - not too strong, not too weak, just perfect. They definitely didn't skimp on the ingredients either, everything tasted top-notch. We also tried the tomato bruschetta and the halloumi bruschetta. Both were amazing, especially the bread - you could tell it was freshly baked, warm and soft. The wedges were a hit too, super crispy and addictive. The whole restaurant had a great atmosphere. The music was nice and relaxing, and we sat outside surrounded by trees. It felt like a little oasis in the city. Our waiter, Elie, was awesome - really friendly and helpful. The prices were very reasonable relative to the huge portion and especially compared to restaurants in Beirut. Overall, Provincial is a must-visit!

A Culinary Gem in Hamra: Mezyan Restaurant Nestled in the heart of Hamra, Beirut, Mezyan Restaurant is a shining beacon of Mediterranean and Lebanese gastronomy. Under the astute management of Mansour Aziz and Jad Hamdan, this culinary haven has carved a niche for itself, offering a delightful fusion of flavors in a warm and inviting ambiance. From the moment you step through the doors, you're greeted with a friendly welcome from the efficient staff, setting the tone for an exceptional dining experience. The cozy atmosphere envelops you, creating the perfect backdrop for indulging in a culinary journey like no other. Mezyan's bar is a destination in itself, boasting an impressive array of savory drinks crafted with precision and care. Whether you're in the mood for a classic cocktail or an innovative concoction, the skilled bartenders are ready to cater to your every whim. As you make your way to the restaurant area, you're presented with a menu that promises culinary delights beyond compare. Each dish is a masterpiece, carefully crafted to tantalize your taste buds and leave you craving for more. From traditional Lebanese mezze to innovative Mediterranean creations, every plate is a testament to the culinary prowess of the chefs at Mezyan. What truly sets Mezyan apart is its commitment to providing top-notch service at reasonable prices. Despite its reputation for excellence, Mezyan remains accessible to all, ensuring that everyone can experience the magic of its cuisine. Adding to the allure of Mezyan are the occasional bands that grace the stage, entertaining guests with soulful melodies and infectious rhythms. It's the perfect accompaniment to an already unforgettable dining experience, elevating it to new heights of enjoyment. In addition to its regular offerings, Mezyan also caters to tailor-made events, ensuring that every celebration is imbued with the same level of care and attention to detail that has become synonymous with the restaurant. Whether you're dining solo or with a group, reservations at Mezyan are highly recommended to ensure you secure a spot in this culinary paradise. The restaurant attracts a diverse clientele, with both locals and foreigners from all walks of life coming together to savor its delights. In conclusion, Mezyan Restaurant is a true gem in the bustling neighborhood of Hamra. With its delectable cuisine, cozy ambiance, and top-notch service, it's a place where culinary dreams come to life. Whether you're a seasoned food enthusiast or simply looking for an unforgettable dining experience, Mezyan is sure to exceed your expectations.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at Mezyan, a hidden gem of a mezze restaurant tucked away in Beirut, and let me tell you, it was an experience to remember. From the moment I stepped through the doors, I knew I was in for something special. First and foremost, the food at Mezyan is simply outstanding. Each dish burst with authentic flavours that transported me straight to the heart of Lebanese cuisine. Paired with some delightful local wines, every bite was a culinary adventure that left me craving more. But it's not just the food that makes Mezyan stand out - it's the atmosphere as well. The restaurant boasts an authentic design that captures the essence of Lebanese culture, creating a warm and inviting ambience that instantly makes you feel at home. Sure, finding the place might be a bit of a challenge, as you need to enter via the big hall of another building, but trust me, it's well worth the effort. One dish that particularly stood out to me was the kibbe - it was simply amazing. Perfectly seasoned and expertly prepared, it was a true testament to the skill and dedication of the chefs at Mezyan. Of course, great food is only part of the equation - service is equally important, and Mezyan certainly delivers in that department. The staff were attentive, friendly, and knowledgeable, ensuring that every aspect of my dining experience was nothing short of perfect. And let's not forget about the prices - for the quality of the food and service you receive, the prices at Mezyan are incredibly smart. You'll leave feeling satisfied both in your stomach and in your wallet, which is always a win in my book. In conclusion, if you're looking for an unforgettable dining experience in Beirut that combines amazing food, an authentic atmosphere, and excellent service, look no further than Mezyan. Trust me, you won't be disappointed.

Located in the heart of the city, our favorite Lebanese high-end restaurant offers an unparalleled dining experience that tantalizes the senses from start to finish. From the moment you step through the elegant entrance, you're greeted with an ambiance that seamlessly blends sophistication with warm Lebanese hospitality. Although Em sheriff is known to be one of the nicest restaurants in downtown Beirut, I hadn’t gotten around to visiting until recently. I absolutely adore Bar Tartine! After being abroad for some time, I was thrilled to return and find that the restaurant still maintains its exceptional quality and taste, if not even better. From the moment we stepped inside, we were greeted with warm smiles and a welcoming atmosphere. The interior design is chic and modern, with stylish decor and comfortable seating arrangements that immediately put us at ease. Our waitress, Setrida, was an absolute gem. She displayed a perfect balance of professionalism and friendliness, taking amazing care of us throughout our visit. She patiently answered all our questions about the menu and provided excellent recommendations based on our preferences. Her attentiveness and genuine interest in ensuring our dining experience was top-notch made us feel valued and appreciated as customers. Now, let's talk about the food. Oh my goodness, it was beyond delicious! The menu offers a diverse range of options, from classic favorites to creative and innovative dishes. Each bite was a burst of flavor and a true delight for the taste buds. The attention to detail in every dish was evident, and the presentation was nothing short of stunning. We couldn't help but savor every moment of our meal. Despite the incredible quality of the food, the bill was surprisingly reasonable. Considering the portion sizes and the level of craftsmanship that goes into the dishes, we felt like we were getting exceptional value for our money. Bar Tartine truly understands the importance of providing an affordable yet memorable dining experience. One aspect that stood out to us was the cozy and inviting atmosphere. The lighting was soft and warm, creating a relaxed ambiance that was perfect for a casual catch-up with friends or a romantic date night. The restaurant was bustling with a lively energy, yet it never felt overcrowded or noisy. We were able to enjoy our conversations without any distractions, allowing us to fully immerse ourselves in the dining experience. In conclusion, I highly recommend Bar Tartine for brunch, lunch, and dinner without a doubt. It is a haven for food lovers, where exceptional quality, attentive service, reasonable pricing, and a cozy atmosphere come together to create a truly enjoyable dining experience. Whether you're a local or a visitor, Bar Tartine is a must-visit destination that will leave you wanting to come back for more. Near the place and valet Kid-friendliness: I saw some families with their kids, no playground or stuff to play with but it surely it can be a family and kid friendly place as well.

Zomato and The peninsula management hosted us, a bunch of eager foodies, for a zomato meetup. Escape the city's traffic and disconnect, how you may ask? Well it is easy. The peninsula is located in Dbayeh back street before Le Royal Hotel. Take a small turn on the right to be transported to field of gardenia and cheerful smiles. Behind the big wooden door you enter the villa where attention has been given to the details to stay faithful to the Italian theme. Walk even further and there you will find a terrace looking over the garden where they host on Thursdays themed nights animated by dancers and a lavish buffet of Italian delicacies. Now back to the essential, the food experience! First things first; the warm bread basket / box wrapped with green cloth and served with a side of marinated tomatoes: et voila you can make your own fresh bruschetta! The menu had different kinds of salads: Insalata della casa: a beautiful presentation and rich ingredients, though I always prefer the cherry tomatoes over regular ones. The meat is succulent and cooked as per my request medium rare. Thank you guys for the high standard service, the tasty food and the pleasant conversation. And my lovely readers, what are you waiting for, pick up the phone and reserve asap to the cheapest trip to Italy!

During my recent visit to S&1/2, I had a mixed experience. While the food was very good, there were some issues with the service. This was my first time at this branch, and there were so many orders and noises that it was difficult to enjoy the atmosphere. We ordered the chicken escalope sandwich, shawarma shaker, and fries box, all for $10. Before we ordered, the staff told us we would have to wait 30 minutes, which was okay with us. We placed our order at 8:48 pm. At 9:02 pm, the sandwich was done, and at 9:27 pm, the shaker was done, which was surprising since shakers are supposed to be a fast meal. All of our orders were being prepared for delivery, which may have contributed to the delay. While the food was tasty, I found the sauce to be spicy. It would be great if the restaurant could take into consideration that not everyone likes spicy meals. Also, the fries were good, but the portions were small. Overall, I had a mixed experience at this restaurant, but I would be willing to give it another try in the future.

I recently had the pleasure of dining at an Egyptian restaurant that truly transported me to the heart of Egypt's culinary delights. From the moment I stepped in, I was enchanted by the warm and inviting atmosphere that enveloped the entire space. Let's talk about the food—it was exceptional in every sense. Each dish was a work of art, meticulously prepared with authentic Egyptian flavors and spices that tantalized my taste buds. The Oxtail was succulent and bursting with flavor, a testament to the chef's mastery of the grill. What truly elevated my dining experience was the impeccable service. The staff were not only attentive and knowledgeable about the menu but also exuded a genuine passion for sharing their culture through food. Their recommendations were spot on, and they went above and beyond to ensure that every aspect of my meal was perfect. The atmosphere of the restaurant was another highlight. The decor transported me to the bustling streets of Cairo, with vibrant colors, intricate patterns, and soft Egyptian music playing in the background. It was the perfect backdrop for a memorable dining experience, whether you're looking for a cozy dinner for two or a lively gathering with friends and family. In conclusion, this Egyptian restaurant is a gem that deserves to be celebrated. With exceptional food, great staff, and an amazing atmosphere, it's a must-visit for anyone craving an authentic taste of Egypt's culinary heritage. Special thanks to Yaseer , Emad and Amr.

A lovely place down by the river. Even when everywhere else seemed quiet this place was busy with both locals and tourists which is always a good sign. Service was very quick and professional - no hidden charges. We shared a few dishes: tahini, garlic bread, chicken shawarma, baba ganoush and tomato soup. A mix. The tahini was nice and seemed fresh, shawarma was very tasty but the fries with it were cold. The soup was nice and tasty and the ganoush also. Garlic bread a bit disappointing - I wouldn’t have ordered this again. It seemed like a store bought loaf with some cheese and pepper over baked on. Felt cheap when the free bread they gave with the tahini was far nicer. Views of the Nile are there, but not remarkable. You’re mostly blocked by a group of feluccas and taxi boats. Overall a good restaurant and we would definitely return. Kid-friendliness: Not built for kids but not really bad for them either. There were some there with no issue.
